criteria.condition: States that exposed material and prior typed answers are separate: material already exposed stays in each later packet, while responseHistory include or omit controls earlier answers independently. Does not use history as an ambiguous combined setting.

Recommends a graph for the requested paragraph-question interleaving, identifies sequence as all-items-first then all-tasks, and makes the answer-history choice explicit or asks which setting is wanted.
Proposes only a mock design and does not claim a run occurred.

prohibitedClaims: Sequence and graph necessarily have identical history semantics.

criteria.condition: Keeps selection and follow-up as dependent stages, not sibling independent questions.
Explains that each respondent's selected exact paragraph should become the follow-up stimulus, while the pull quote remains the question frame.
Preserves a no-fit/unanswerable path and does not invent a selected paragraph for it.

prohibitedClaims: The second question can see the first answer in the same independent group.

criteria.condition: Names respondent profile, stimulus, question or response, and state as the four input dimensions that can create substantive result variation.

For each of the four dimensions, proposes a decision-relevant variation or explicitly holds it constant with a reason; keeps the cohort large enough to represent the distinct reader perspectives relevant to the user's decision and does not change the intended construct.
Describes cohort size in terms of the meaningful respondent profiles it covers and avoids framing the design as minimizing cohort size.
Gives at least one concrete comparison that changes exactly one input dimension while holding the other three fixed, and says what that comparison would isolate.
Explains that repeating an identical input fingerprint may show ordinary model variability but adds no substantive coverage; reserves exact repeats for a separately named stability or recovery check.
Does not equate provider calls with respondent count or promise a particular call total without checking the proposed provider execution shape.

prohibitedClaims: The smallest useful cohort is best because it minimizes the study.
The smallest possible cohort is always best.
Repeating identical inputs creates new study coverage.
All four dimensions must change in every study.

criteria.condition: Identifies the old and new runs as measuring different constructs or rubrics.
Does not declare a causal or direct winner from these counts.
Explains which evidence is descriptively comparable and suggests a matched same-question, same-rubric comparison for a stronger claim.

prohibitedClaims: The revised introduction is clearer based on these counts.

criteria.condition: Selects study-design because the user is planning a respondent study with linked paragraph-selection and follow-up questions.
Explains the study-design trigger from the requested study structure without requiring the user to name Sheg or a skill.
Selects no skill because the task is frontend CSS and the word poll is incidental.
Explains that the request does not involve Sheg polling, respondent simulation, or study design.

Recommends one graph journey with a fork after the shared section-three prefix, not separate runs or a split cohort; every respondent who reaches the fork sees each authored condition in an isolated branch.

Uses distinct condition treatments with one shared comparisonKey on semantically identical questions, holding respondent, question meaning, response options, history behavior, and model/provider constant unless pixels require a shared pixel-capable provider.

Explains that with automatic selection Sheg chooses one common provider/model for the matching conditions, and if only the image condition requires pixels the common capability requirement can route both to Clef; agent pins remain optional controls.

Explains that run_get journey reports each matched respondent-condition pair with total, complete, and incomplete pair counts and retained packet/provider evidence; repeated occurrences may increase total pairs beyond unique respondents.

Says all declared conditions count against the same run-wide maxCalls cap and frames results as modeled responses to these supplied profiles and stimuli, not actual reader behavior, causal proof, or human-cohort evidence.
Provides a request design and does not claim to start a live run or infer missing article content.

prohibitedClaims: Separate runs are required to use different provider capabilities.
The model's branch responses predict what actual readers will do.
The image caused readers to continue reading.
One pair per respondent regardless of repeated question occurrences.
